Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Incus daemon (incusd) spawns backup compressor with argument-injection flags (--pass-through/-o) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-48755: Incus has an argument injection in backup comp

Incus daemon (incusd) spawns backup compressor with argument-injection flags (--pass-through/-o) AIExploitation High
Hunts CVE-2026-48755: incusd invokes an allow-listed compressor (zstd/gzip/xz/etc.) for a direct backup passing ONLY '-c', but attacker-controlled compression_algorithm smuggles extra tokens. A compressor child of incusd carrying a file-write flag (--pass-through, -o, --output) is the argument-injection primitive — legitimate compression-to-stdout never uses those. Rationale: Keys on the exact article primitive: incusd (root daemon) → allow-listed compressor whose cmdline carries --pass-through/-o/--output. Backup compression writes to stdout, so these output flags are exclusively the injection payload. Cross-checked GHSA-v6mj-8pf4-hhw4 and Snyk Labs Incus write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-v6mj-8pf4-hhw4 • https://labs.snyk.io/resources/incus-vulnerabilities-newline-symlink-arbitrary-writes/ • https://vulnerability.circl.lu/vuln/ghsa-v6mj-8pf4-hhw4
ATT&CKT1190 T1202
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Newer/patched Incus (>=7.2.0) that has removed the vuln — should no longer emit compressor children with these flags; a hit post-patch warrants investigation
  • Custom operator-defined compression_algorithm using legitimate tuning flags like 'zstd -19 -T0' (does NOT contain -o/--pass-through, so filtered)
  • A wrapper compressor script an admin registered that internally forwards -o for its own output handling
  • Backup restore/import which runs the compressor with '-d' to stdout (no -o), correctly excluded by requiring an output flag
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine contains "/var/lib/incus/backups/")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Pull the full CompressorCmd — confirm it contains an explicit output path (-o/--output/--pass-through) pointing at a host location outside /var/lib/incus/backups (e.g. /etc/cron.d/). Note the DeviceName and the Incus version via DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate the host; stop incusd; block API port 8443 at the firewall and revoke any client certs/tokens that authenticated the offending /backups request. Delete any attacker-written host file. 3) HUNT: Pivot to UC2 (compressor writing to /etc). Review incusd access logs for POST /1.0/instances/*/backups with anomalous compression_algorithm, and check /etc/cron.d, /etc/systemd/system, /root/.ssh for freshly written entries. Upgrade to Incus v7.2.0.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "incusd"
| where FileName in~ ("zstd","gzip","xz","lz4","lzma","bzip2","pigz","pzstd","pxz","tar2sqfs")
// incusd passes only '-c' (+ optional level/thread) for backup compression; -o/--pass-through/--output are file-write injection primitives
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "--pass-through"
    or ProcessCommandLine contains " -o "
    or ProcessCommandLine contains "--output"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          CompressorImage = FolderPath,
          CompressorCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has "incusd"
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("zstd","gzip","xz","lz4","lzma","bzip2","pigz","pzstd","pxz","tar2sqfs")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine contains "--pass-through"
    or TargetProcessCommandLine contains " -o "
    or TargetProcessCommandLine contains "--output"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Incus Daemon Spawns Compressor With Argument-Injection Flag
id: 4c8f1a52-7d3e-4b19-9a2c-1f0e6b7d5a01
description: Detects CVE-2026-48755 argument injection where incusd invokes an allow-listed backup compressor carrying a file-write flag (--pass-through/-o/--output) that legitimate compression-to-stdout never uses.
references:
  - https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-v6mj-8pf4-hhw4
  - https://labs.snyk.io/resources/incus-vulnerabilities-newline-symlink-arbitrary-writes/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/07
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1202
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '/incusd'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/zstd'
      - '/gzip'
      - '/xz'
      - '/lz4'
      - '/lzma'
      - '/bzip2'
      - '/pigz'
      - '/pzstd'
      - '/pxz'
      - '/tar2sqfs'
  selection_flag:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--pass-through'
      - ' -o '
      - '--output'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_flag
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.name:(zstd OR gzip OR xz OR lz4 OR lzma OR bzip2 OR pigz OR pzstd OR pxz OR tar2sqfs) (@process.command_line:*--pass-through* OR @process.command_line:*--output* OR @process.command_line:*\ -o\ *)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/incusd$/i
| ImageFileName=/\/(zstd|gzip|xz|lz4|lzma|bzip2|pigz|pzstd|pxz|tar2sqfs)$/i
| regex("(--pass-through|--output|\\s-o\\s)", field=CommandLine)
| table([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name=incusd (Processes.process_name IN ("zstd","gzip","xz","lz4","lzma","bzip2","pigz","pzstd","pxz","tar2sqfs")) (Processes.process="*--pass-through*" OR Processes.process="* -o *" OR Processes.process="*--output*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name=incusd (Processes.process_name IN ("zstd","gzip","xz","lz4","lzma","bzip2","pigz","pzstd","pxz","tar2sqfs")) (Processes.process="*--pass-through*" OR Processes.process="* -o *" OR Processes.process="*--output*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Backup compressor (child of incusd) writes to a sensitive host persistence path AIInstallation High
Hunts the AFW→RCE stage of CVE-2026-48755: the argument-injected compressor (zstd --pass-through -o ...) lands an attacker file on the host as root. Fires when an allow-listed compressor writes into cron, systemd, sudoers, SSH or profile paths — the PoC drops /etc/cron.d/incus-zstd-rce. A backup compressor writing to /etc is never legitimate. Rationale: Second, independent pivot (file-landing rather than cmdline): a member of the article's exact compressor allow-list writing into /etc/cron.d (the PoC's /etc/cron.d/incus-zstd-rce), systemd, sudoers.d, /root/.ssh or /etc/ld.so.preload. Compressors never legitimately write to these host paths. Corroborated via GHSA-v6mj-8pf4-hhw4 and Snyk Labs. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-v6mj-8pf4-hhw4 • https://labs.snyk.io/resources/incus-vulnerabilities-newline-symlink-arbitrary-writes/ • https://vulnerability.circl.lu/vuln/ghsa-v6mj-8pf4-hhw4
ATT&CKT1053.003 T1543.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • An admin manually piping a config archive through zstd/gzip into /etc via a shell (rare; check parent is a login shell, not incusd)
  • Configuration-management tooling (Ansible/Salt) that stages a compressed unit file and decompresses it into /etc/systemd/system — verify the invoking user/parent
  • A packaging or backup-restore job that legitimately expands archives into /etc profile scripts
  • Security tooling test/validation writing sample cron files during a controlled exercise
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "incusd"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Open the written file (FolderPath/FileName) — a cron entry running '/bin/sh -c', a rogue systemd unit, an added sudoers rule or authorized_keys line confirms RCE/persistence. Confirm the Writer's parent is incusd (InitiatingProcessParentFileName). 2) CONTAIN: Isolate the host, stop incusd, delete the written persistence file, kill any process/cron spawned from it, and rotate root SSH keys and any credentials reachable from the box. Revoke the Incus client cert/token used. 3) HUNT: Correlate with UC1 for the injected compressor cmdline; review /etc/cron.d, /etc/systemd/system, /etc/sudoers.d, /root/.ssh across all Incus hosts; audit incusd for backup requests with crafted compression_algorithm. Patch to Incus v7.2.0.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("zstd","gzip","xz","lz4","lzma","bzip2","pigz","pzstd","pxz","tar2sqfs")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/etc/cron.d/","/etc/cron.daily/","/etc/cron.hourly/","/etc/systemd/system/","/etc/sudoers.d/","/root/.ssh/","/etc/profile.d/","/etc/ld.so.preload")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          Writer = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          FolderPath, FileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("zstd","gzip","xz","lz4","lzma","bzip2","pigz","pzstd","pxz","tar2sqfs")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/etc/cron.d/","/etc/cron.daily/","/etc/cron.hourly/","/etc/systemd/system/","/etc/sudoers.d/","/root/.ssh/","/etc/profile.d/","/etc/ld.so.preload")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Incus S3 multipart uploadId path traversal request (CVE-2026-48753) AIExploitation High
Hunts inbound PUT requests to the Incus S3 bucket endpoint whose uploadId query parameter carries directory-traversal sequences (../ or URL-encoded ..%2F), the exploit signature for CVE-2026-48753. This is the on-the-wire primitive that lets an authenticated bucket user write arbitrary host files. Rationale: Anchored on the exact PoC request shape from the advisory: PUT to the bucket with partNumber + uploadId=../../../../etc/cron.d (URL-encoded ..%2F). Traversal in an S3 uploadId has no legitimate use, giving very low FP. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-ccjc-4qc3-jxqc • https://vulnerability.circl.lu/vuln/ghsa-ccjc-4qc3-jxqc
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security scanners (Nessus/Burp/Nuclei) firing path-traversal templates against the Incus S3 endpoint
  • Internal red-team / pentest validating CVE-2026-48753 remediation
  • S3 client SDK sending an oddly-encoded but legitimate uploadId that happens to include '..' in a key name (rare)
  • DAST tooling in CI pipelines probing the storage_buckets_address port
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in ("10.10.10.10")  // exclude known authorized scanner / pentest source IPs
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the target host runs Incus < 7.1.0 with core.storage_buckets_address set; decode the uploadId in RequestURL to see the traversal target (e.g. /etc/cron.d). Identify SourceIP and whether the S3 credentials used are known. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the proxy/WAF, rotate/revoke the storage bucket access keys, and restrict or firewall the S3 bucket port. Upgrade Incus to >=7.1.0. 3) Hunt: pivot to file-write and cron-execution detections on the same host (below) to confirm whether a file actually landed in /etc/cron.d or other sensitive paths.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod =~ "PUT"
| where RequestURL has "uploadId" and RequestURL has "partNumber"
| where RequestURL has_any ("..%2F", "..%2f", "../", "%2E%2E%2F", "..%252F")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, DeviceAction
| order by TimeGenerated desc

incusd process writing to /etc/cron.d or other sensitive host paths (CVE-2026-48753) AIInstallation High
Hunts the Incus daemon (incusd) creating or modifying files under system directories it should never touch — /etc/cron.d, /etc/sudoers.d, /etc/systemd/system, /root/.ssh, ld.so.preload. This is the post-exploitation file-write primitive of CVE-2026-48753 regardless of the specific payload. Rationale: incusd is a storage/container daemon whose legitimate writes stay inside its storage pool directory; any write to /etc/cron.d or /root/.ssh is the exploit outcome. Path list mirrors the advisory's /etc/cron.d target plus adjacent root-RCE sinks. Datadog left empty — the provided linux.auditd schema exposes no file-target path field. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-ccjc-4qc3-jxqc • https://vulnerability.circl.lu/vuln/ghsa-ccjc-4qc3-jxqc
ATT&CKT1053.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Incus package upgrade/postinstall touching /etc/systemd/system for its own unit files (verify parent is dpkg/rpm, not incusd itself)
  • Admin manually running incus with elevated config that legitimately regenerates a systemd unit
  • EDR mis-attribution of a helper child process to incusd on busy hosts
  • Backup/restore of a storage volume whose contents coincidentally include cron-like filenames (path would still be inside the pool dir, not /etc)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName != "" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("dpkg","rpm","apt","dnf","yum")
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the written file's contents (e.g. /etc/cron.d/*) for a cron line invoking /bin/sh or a reverse shell; confirm incusd version < 7.1.0 and that InitiatingProcess is genuinely incusd, not the package manager. 2) Contain: delete the malicious file, kill any process it spawned, revoke the S3 bucket credentials, and isolate the host. Upgrade Incus to >=7.1.0. 3) Hunt: correlate with the S3 traversal-request detection for the originating SourceIP/credentials, and search for cron-spawned shells or the marker file dropped by the payload across the fleet.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "incusd"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/etc/cron.d","/etc/cron.daily","/etc/cron.hourly","/etc/cron.weekly","/etc/cron.monthly","/etc/crontab","/var/spool/cron","/etc/sudoers.d","/etc/systemd/system","/root/.ssh","/etc/ld.so.preload","/etc/passwd","/etc/shadow")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has "incusd"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileCreate","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/etc/cron.d","/etc/cron.daily","/etc/cron.hourly","/etc/crontab","/var/spool/cron","/etc/sudoers.d","/etc/systemd/system","/root/.ssh","/etc/ld.so.preload","/etc/passwd","/etc/shadow")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cron-spawned shell that deletes its own /etc/cron.d entry (Incus CVE-2026-48753 payload) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts a shell launched by cron whose command line removes a file from /etc/cron.d (self-cleaning run-once cron) or drops the PoC marker file, the execution stage of the CVE-2026-48753 chain where the traversal-written cron job fires as root and cleans up after itself. Rationale: Derived from the advisory PoC cron body: '* * * * * root /bin/sh -c "id > /incus-s3-uploadid-bash-rce; rm -f /etc/cron.d/part-00001"'. A cron job that deletes its own /etc/cron.d file after one run is a strong run-once-exploit tell; the marker string is an exact PoC IOC. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/lxc/incus/security/advisories/GHSA-ccjc-4qc3-jxqc • https://vulnerability.circl.lu/vuln/ghsa-ccjc-4qc3-jxqc
ATT&CKT1053.003 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate provisioning/config-management (Ansible/cloud-init) that deploys a run-once cron.d job which self-deletes
  • Package post-install scripts that clean up transient cron.d drop-ins
  • Admin one-off maintenance cron that removes itself after execution
  • Log-rotation or housekeeping cron that legitimately rm's files under /etc/cron.d during cleanup
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ansible","cloud-init","puppet","chef","salt"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full ActingProcessCommandLine and any child processes; check whether the executing user is root and whether the cron file originated from an incusd write (correlate with the file-write detection). 2) Contain: if malicious, kill the process tree, remove residual cron.d entries and any dropped marker/payload files, rotate S3 bucket keys, and isolate the host. Patch Incus to >=7.1.0. 3) Hunt: sweep the fleet for the marker file /incus-s3-uploadid-bash-rce and for any other cron.d files written by incusd, and review S3 endpoint access logs for the traversal request that seeded this.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cron","crond")
| where (ProcessCommandLine has "/etc/cron.d/" and ProcessCommandLine has "rm ") or ProcessCommandLine has "incus-s3-uploadid"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("cron","crond")
| where (ActingProcessCommandLine has "/etc/cron.d/" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "rm ") or ActingProcessCommandLine has "incus-s3-uploadid"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE ((@process.command_line:*rm* AND @process.command_line:*\/etc\/cron.d\/*) OR @process.command_line:*incus-s3-uploadid*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^cron[d]?$/i
| (regex("/etc/cron\\.d/", field=CommandLine) AND regex("\\brm\\b", field=CommandLine)) OR regex("incus-s3-uploadid", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("cron","crond") ((Processes.process="*rm *" AND Processes.process="*/etc/cron.d/*") OR Processes.process="*incus-s3-uploadid*") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("cron","crond") ((Processes.process="*rm *" AND Processes.process="*/etc/cron.d/*") OR Processes.process="*incus-s3-uploadid*") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| sort - lastTime
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48753")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-48753")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-48753")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-48753")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-48753: Incus has an arbitrary file write via path tra Installation High
Auto-generated hunt targeting the specific binaries, paths, registry locations and command-line fragments named in this article. Hunting tier — needs analyst review and environment tuning before promotion to alerting.
ATT&CKT1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Registry
// Article-specific bespoke detection — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-48753: Incus has an arbitrary file write via path tra
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/usr/bin/env", "/etc/cron.d", "/etc/cron.d/part-00001"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
